name: Hospitalcore

influenced_by: weirdcore and traumacore's unsettling, found-image internet aesthetics
clinical medical photography and institutional interior design

reacts_against: sanitized, comforting imagery generally, presenting the specific sterility of clinical spaces (fluorescent light, hospital green, medical equipment) as a deliberately unsettling visual mood rather than something to avoid depicting.
article: Hospitalcore is a niche 2020s internet-aesthetic tag that draws its palette and props directly from clinical medical settings — hospital green walls, harsh fluorescent light, exposed medical equipment — sitting within the broader weirdcore and traumacore family of unsettling, found-image internet aesthetics rather than functioning as a wearable fashion look the way most entries in this archive do. Its documentation is thin even by the standards of recent internet-aesthetic tags, circulating mainly within Aesthetics Wiki and adjacent fan communities rather than receiving sustained mainstream trend coverage. Like several aesthetics in the weirdcore family, hospitalcore trades on a specific, culturally loaded discomfort — hospitals are spaces most people associate with illness, loss of control and institutional authority — turning that discomfort into a deliberate visual mood rather than something imagery conventionally tries to soften or avoid.

findings: light — about 52% of the measured color is pale or near-white
mostly muted — about 94% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from Wikimedia Commons images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
